open-question.question: When the recommend sweep dispatches nothing — every block already carries a recommendation, or every dispatched question was still skipped after its repair — should it still run the tool's sort and commit any reorder under Question-ordering, or is the sort step reached only after at least one successful embed?
open-question.alternative: The sort is a fixed end-of-run step reached by every run that found questions — step 1b's empty print and an all-skipped dispatch loop both fall through to it instead of exiting to the no-op line — with the dirty-own-path guard as its only no-op test, so a run commits a Question-ordering commit exactly when the sort moved a block. The sweep gains an unconditional postcondition — the document is sorted after every run — and a bare re-run becomes the one way to restore order once the answer path has disturbed it: the goal makes the sweep the sole sorter and no other write reorders, and an agreeing answer untags a dependent into an origin that keeps sitting behind a still-dependent block (verified against the tool's own remove_question and walk_order: the all-annotated document B, C, D walks as B, D, C), a drift only a no-dispatch sort can repair; on an already-sorted document the sort is the identity, so the idempotent re-run still commits nothing and costs one tool call. A run that annotated nothing can still produce a lone Question-ordering commit, so the sweep's no-op story gains a second cause — the report step must tell "nothing changed" from "only the order changed", which is exactly the still-open sibling "Report line when only the sort commits" and keeps it live — and the recorded invariant "a sweep that annotated nothing commits nothing" narrows to "annotated nothing and moved nothing".

The sort step is gated on at least one successful embed in this run — a run whose step-1b list was empty, or whose every dispatch was still skipped after its repair, exits to the no-op line without calling sort — so a Question-ordering commit can only ever follow a Recommendation-annotation commit of the same run. A no-dispatch run stays a pure no-op with one cause and one line, the present step-1b early exit and step-5 no-op wording survive unchanged, and the sibling "Report line when only the sort commits" is mooted because its scenario cannot arise. Sortedness then holds only at the moment of annotation: an all-annotated document the answer path left out of walk order, or stripped blocks stranded mid-document by a strip-then-all-skipped run, stay that way, and with the sweep the sole sorter there is no way to restore order short of a strip-and-regenerate detour that discards a recommendation or a review pass that happens to add a question — the goal's reading-order promise silently lapses with no remedy.

The sort opens step 4 and runs whenever the dispatch loop ran at all — an all-skipped run still sorts — while step 1b's empty print keeps its early exit straight to the no-op line, so an all-annotated document is never re-sorted. It is the smallest edit — the goal's "once after its last dispatch" taken literally, the step-1b exit untouched — and it still tidies the one drift an all-skipped run leaves, moving blocks a strip stranded mid-document to the end. The rule is keyed on an incidental control-flow fact rather than a property anyone can rely on: the all-annotated document that drifted through the answer path — the only case a no-dispatch sort can repair — is exactly the case it excludes, so it delivers neither the first option's postcondition nor the second's clean no-op, and the report step still needs the only-the-sort-committed line.
open-question.recommendation: A guard-protected sort on every run is the one mode-free rule that makes "sorted after the sweep" a postcondition rather than a moment, and a bare re-run is the only repair the goal leaves for the order the answer path's tag drops and strips disturb, while on a sorted document the sort is the identity so the idempotent no-op run still commits nothing.

open-question.question: The per-question annotation commit carries the lifted recommendation line as its body, but the shared commit procedure takes only PATHS and SUBJECT: should it gain an optional BODY input that every caller may supply, or should the recommend sweep pass the body ad hoc while still following the procedure for the guard and path-scoped staging?
open-question.alternative: Add a third, optional input BODY to the shared commit procedure's Inputs — zero or more body lines the caller supplies — and have its step 3 commit with git commit -m "<SUBJECT>" -m "<BODY>" when one is given and subject-only otherwise, so the recommend sweep hands over the lifted "<option> — <rationale>" line per question exactly as it hands over PATHS and SUBJECT. It makes the contract match the practice already in the tree: answer-open-question, answer-open-question-with-alternative, answer-open-question-with-recommendation, and capture-milestone-principle-updates each already pass the procedure a Body bullet (capture even says "three inputs" and restates the -m/-m command form itself) while the procedure's Inputs section declares two and its step 3 only nods to bodies in a parenthetical — the sweep would be the fifth ad hoc case; declaring the input once keeps how a body reaches git inside the single source of truth, and the optional shape lets the sweep's two commits (per-question Recommendation-annotation with a body, Question-ordering without) and the nine body-less callers all pass through one procedure without any of them changing. It widens the shared file's input contract and the CLAUDE.md line and requirements prose that describe it as PATHS-and-SUBJECT, so the change reaches beyond the sweep this milestone is editing, and a declared third input invites a fourth later unless the bar is stated with it — an input is a git commit argument the caller resolves, never a policy the procedure decides.

alternative.id: Ad hoc body in the sweep

open-question.alternative: Keep the procedure's Inputs at PATHS and SUBJECT and have the recommend sweep add a Body bullet of its own — the lifted line — leaning on step 3's "plus any body lines the caller supplies" parenthetical, exactly as the four body-supplying callers do today. Zero change to the shared procedure, its CLAUDE.md description, or any other caller: the sweep's commit step reads like the three answer skills' and the milestone's edit stays confined to the sweep. It entrenches a contract-versus-practice split — five callers passing three inputs to a procedure whose contract declares two — with the way a body reaches git restated per caller (capture already spells out the -m/-m form) rather than owned by the single source of truth, so every future body-supplying caller re-decides the shape and a reader of the contract alone never learns bodies are supported.

Drop the procedure reference from the sweep's commit step and inline the guard, the path-scoped git add, and a git commit -m "<subject>" -m "<body>" per question, the way answer-all-open-questions-with-recommendation and complete-all-tasks commit. The sweep would read line for line like its sibling per-item orchestrator — the answer sweep the goal says it mirrors — with its body handling visible in place and no shared-file dependency at all. Those two orchestrators inline only because an agent already staged the index; the sweep is itself the writer with nothing staged, so it is exactly the path-scoped stage-and-guard case the procedure exists for — inlining would copy that mechanics into a third place and break the rule, stated in CLAUDE.md and docs/workflow.md, that every committing skill references the one shared procedure.
open-question.recommendation: The body is already a de facto third input for four callers and the sweep makes it five, so the one honest fix is to declare it optional in the procedure that is the single source of truth for the commit step — one edit that also lets the sweep's with-body annotation commit and its body-less ordering commit share one unchanged path.

open-question.id: Report line when only the sort commits
open-question.question: When a run embeds nothing but the final sort reorders the document and commits, which console line does the sweep print — the terse success line, the distinct nothing-annotated no-op line, or a third line — given that the success line reads as if recommendations were embedded?
open-question.alternative: Keep step 5 keyed on whether the run committed anything: a reorder-only run passed the ordering commit's guard, so it is a success path and prints the unchanged fixed line `Recommendations embedded.`, leaving the Question-ordering commit to git as its only record. Nothing in the report step or the terse-reporting invariant changes — one success line, one no-op line — and the selection rule stays the simplest possible: any commit prints the success line, no commit prints the no-op line. The line is false on exactly the runs it now covers: under an every-run sort an all-annotated document the answer path left out of walk order reorders with zero dispatches, and a strip-then-all-skipped run reorders while every dispatched question is listed as skipped in the advisory printed right under it — so the console says recommendations were embedded when none were, and a user reading that line as the cue to run the answer sweep is misled.

Treat the ordering commit as housekeeping outside the sweep's reportable outcome: a run in which no embed wrote prints the distinct nothing-annotated line — reworded from "nothing changed, nothing committed" to "no recommendation was embedded" plus its usual reason — whether or not the sort committed, leaving the Question-ordering commit to git. It reports the one decision-critical fact — there is nothing new to answer — with the line already reserved for it, and the reorder, being recorded in git, fails the git-absent half of the advisory test and so earns no console mention by the plugin's own rule. It makes a committing run print the no-op line: every current form of that line says nothing was committed while a Question-ordering commit just landed, the invariant defines the line by the dirty-own-path guard having fired while one guard passed, and the rewording needed to keep it true — key it on the embed guard, drop "nothing committed" — turns it into a third line in all but name while blurring the no-op concept every other committing skill shares.

Add a second fixed terse success line for the sweep, `Questions reordered.`, printed when no embed wrote but the sort's Question-ordering commit landed; step 5 then picks by a strict order — an embed wrote: `Recommendations embedded.`; else the sort committed: `Questions reordered.`; else the no-op line with its reason — with the still-skipped advisory alongside whichever line prints. Every line stays true and identifier-free, the success line keeps meaning "there are new recommendations to answer" and the no-op line keeps meaning "nothing was committed", the reorder line reads like its own commit marker so the console matches the git log, and an all-skipped-but-reordered run prints a line the skipped-question advisory beneath it does not contradict. The sweep becomes the one skill with two success lines, so the terse-reporting invariant's "exactly one fixed terse status line" and the docs entry need a carve-out and a stated selection rule, and the string is one more fixed line to keep in sync across CLAUDE.md, docs/skill-reference.md, and both host trees.

Replace `Recommendations embedded.` with one line true of any committing run — `Open questions swept.` or similar — so step 5 keeps exactly two outcomes, the success line whenever either commit landed and the no-op line when neither did. The two-line report step and its invariant survive untouched, and the selection rule stays "did anything commit", with no per-skill carve-out and no third string. The line stops naming what the run did — the one thing a fixed line is for, as `Tasks derived.` and `Recommendations recorded.` show — so the user must open the git log to learn whether there is anything to answer, and the common embed case gives up its accurate line to serve the rare reorder-only one.
open-question.recommendation: With the sort running on every run, a reorder-only run is a real commit that neither existing line describes truthfully, and a second fixed line chosen by what the run committed — embed over reorder over nothing — keeps every line accurate, keeps the success line the cue that there is something to answer, and lets the skipped advisory sit under a line it does not contradict.
